description: RELICTRA is a team of passionate innovators exploring the forgotten history of human space exploration. Through research, creativity, and technology, we aim to uncover the stories behind NASA's abandoned equipment on the Moon and Mars. We believe every forgotten object holds a story worth preserving. We welcome members interested in space science, coding, web development, research, storytelling, UI/UX design, and creative thinking. Together, we bring forgotten missions back to life!
summary:
**Echoes Beyond Earth: The Untold Stories of NASA's Forgotten Spacecraft**

Our project is an interactive 13-page bilingual digital children's storybook in English and Malayalam that explores the history and achievements of NASA's inactive and discarded spacecraft on the Moon, Mars and beyond.

We developed an illustrated storybook featuring 13 historic spacecraft, including Apollo, Surveyor, Viking, Pathfinder, Spirit, Opportunity, Ingenuity, NEAR Shoemaker, Dawn, Kepler and Pioneer 10. It also includes real NASA audio, links to 3D spacecraft models and 360-degree panoramas, printable spacecraft crafts, coloring activities, word searches and an educator guide.

Our project addresses the challenge by transforming NASA's technical mission archives into simple, engaging stories that help children understand what happens to spacecraft after their missions end. It is important because these inactive spacecraft represent valuable scientific discoveries, engineering achievements and milestones in human space exploration. Through this project, we aim to preserve their legacy, promote STEM education and inspire the next generation of space explorers.
details:
Project Details – Abandoned But Not Forgotten

Team: Relictra

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

Our project is an interactive, 13-page illustrated bilingual digital storybook in English and Malayalam designed for children aged 7–11. It introduces inactive and historic NASA spacecraft through the journey of a young stargazer named Mia, who explores what happens to space robots after their missions end.

The storybook covers 13 historic spacecraft and missions across the Moon, Mars, asteroids and deep space. It combines simple storytelling with verified NASA mission facts, real NASA audio, 360-degree panoramas and links to 3D spacecraft models. Children can also participate in hands-on activities such as building a MarCO CubeSat model, coloring, and solving word searches.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Makes complex space science easy for children to understand.
  • Provides learning materials in English and Malayalam.
  • Encourages creativity, curiosity and scientific thinking.
  • Offers free educational resources accessible through digital devices or printed pages.
  • Helps teachers introduce space science through interactive activities.

3. What is the intended impact?

Our main goal is to preserve the legacy of NASA's inactive and discarded spacecraft by sharing their achievements with younger generations. We aim to increase awareness of space exploration, encourage STEM education, promote bilingual learning and inspire children to become future scientists, engineers and space explorers.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware or software were used?

  • Official NASA Science and NSSDCA archives for scientific information.
  • NASA open datasets and mission records for verified facts.
  • NASA Eyes for 3D spacecraft models and space exploration resources.
  • Digital document and illustration tools for creating the storybook and educational materials.
  • PDF format for easy distribution, viewing and printing.

5. How is the project creative?

The project transforms forgotten spacecraft and technical NASA archives into an illustrated storytelling experience. Instead of presenting only scientific facts, it uses a fictional young stargazer named Mia to connect children emotionally with real space missions. Combining bilingual storytelling, authentic NASA media, interactive links and printable STEM activities makes the project educational and engaging.

6. What factors did our team consider?

Our team considered:

  • Age suitability: Simple language and illustrations for children aged 7–11.
  • Accessibility: English and Malayalam language support.
  • Scientific accuracy: Information verified using official NASA and NSSDCA sources.
  • Affordability: A zero-cost PDF that can be viewed or printed.
  • Engagement: Interactive media and hands-on educational activities.
  • Heritage preservation: Respecting inactive spacecraft as important historical achievements and off-world heritage.

Through this project, Team Relictra aims to turn forgotten space missions into inspiring stories for the next generation.
